2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioners, as plaintiffs, filed Other Class Suit No. 206 of 1998 in the court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Ishwardi, against the present opposite parties, as defendant, for a declaration of title contending inter alia, that the schedule-'Ka' property under DS Khatian No. 1237 originally belonged to Mofizuddin Sarder and others. The property was sold in auction in Certificate Case No. 237 of 1943. One Rahmat Ali Sarder purchased the same in auction from whom predecessor of plaintiffs named Rezia Khatun purchased the suit property by registered deed dated 20-3-1944. Property under DS Khatian No. 1364 originally belonged to one Jonaki Nath Paul under whom one Bolai Sarder was borgader, subsequently Jonaki Nath Paul evicted his borgader Bolai Sarder and took the property in his khas possession and sold out the same to Rezia Khatun by registered deed dated 5-5-1945. Rezia Khatun after purchase erected house on a portion of land and was residing therein with her sons and on a part of suit property planted different types of trees and was enjoying the property with the knowledge of all. The defendants have had no title and possession in the suit property. 

 3. Predecessor of the defendant named Azahar Ali Mridha was closely acquainted and related with the predecessor of the plaintiffs, resultantly, entrusted said Azahar Ali Mridha to look after the property and to get the SA khatian prepared in her name and to pay rents to the government. Said Azahar Ali Mridha ensured the predecessor of the plaintiffs that he took proper step for recording name of Rezia Khatun in SA Khatian. Believing Azahar Ali Rezia Khatun kept her relaxed thinking that everything were going well. In the month of August 1998 some of the defendants claimed title in the property saying that they purchased the same from the real owners. The plaintiffs made search to ensure with the concerned authority about the fact and came to know that SA and RS khatians collusively created in the name of predecessor of the defendants. SA and RS khatians wrongly prepared in the name of Azahar Ali Mridha who never acquired the property by any deed from Rezia Khatun. Azahar Ali Mridha taking advantage of looking after the property cunningly prepared the SA and RS khatians in his name instead of Rezia Khatun. Said Rezia Khatun died leaving husband plaintiff No. 1, sons plaintiff Nos. 2-5, grandson by predeceased daughter plaintiff No. 6 and daughter plaintiff No. 7 who inherited the property left by Rezia Khatun and have been possessing the same as their homestead on a part of the suit land and a part of suit land letting out shop to the tenant and running business themselves and planting various trees on the remaining portion of the land without any disturbance from any quarter, but for wrong recording of SA and RS khatians in the name of predecessor of the defendants, title of the plaintiffs have become clouded, hence, the present suit for declaration of title. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1-8 and 10-13 contested the suit by filing two separate written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter din, that the suit is barred by limitation; defect of parties as well as under section 42 of the SR Act. Case of defendant Nos. 1-8 are that the predecessor of plaintiffs Rezia Khatun was owning the property by purchase from whom predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-8 took settlement of the property as agricultural tenant by dakhila. After obtaining settlement Azahar Ali Mridha constructed homestead on a portion of the property and the rest was possessing by planting various trees and cultivating the same. While he was in possession on the basis of settlement from Rezia Khatun SA Khatian correctly recorded in his name. Azahar Ali Mridha have six sons who after getting married, for their residence constructed 16/17 houses thereon and have been leaving with their family. Last RS khatian correctly recorded in the name of Azahar Ali Mridha in the field survey, but along with Azahar Ali Mridha on the back side of khatian name of Rezia Khatun wrongly mentioned for which Azahar Ali Mridha filed objection case under rule 30 of the SAT Rules before the Objection Officer. Rezia Khatun herself appeared in objection case and after hearing concerned Officer accepted the objection and corrected the RS khatian in the name of Azahar Ali Mridha. Thereafter, Rezia Khatun filed appeal case under Rule 31 of the SAT Rules before the Appeal Officer against the order of Settlement Officer. Said Appeal was rejected on contest by judgment and order dated 15-5-1980 affirming the order of Settlement Officer. Thereafter, Rezia Khatun gave up her claim in the property, accordingly, RS khatian finally published in the name of predecessor of the defendant. On the middle north portion of the suit plot Azahar Ali Mridha and his wife have been living by erecting homestead. Other houses constructed subsequently, were let out to the tenants. 

 8. Mr. Md. Alamgir Mostafizur Rahman with Mr. Md. Monjurul Hoque, learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners submit that the trial court as well as the appellate court in dismissing the suit and appeal committed illegality and error of law on misconstruction of evidences and relevant laws in this regard. He submits that the trial court and the appellate court wrongly decided the issue of limitation finding that the plaintiffs were aware about wrong record-of-right in the year 1980 as an objection case was filed by Azahar Ali Mridha against draft RS khatian prepared in the name of Rezia Khatun. 

 9. He argued that cause of action for filing of suit depends on final publication of the record-of-right. In the instant case RS khatian finally published in the year 1992 and the suit was filed in the year 1998, it was very much within time. In support of his such submissions he has referred to the cases of Government of Bangladesh vs AKM Abdul Hye and others reported in 56 DLR (AD) 53 and Government of Bangladesh vs Har Chandra Nath and others reported in 10 MLR (AD) 313 . 

 10. It is further argued that the courts below failed to find that the defendants could not submit any document before the trial court showing that Azahar Ali Mridha obtained settlement of the property from Rezia Khatun by any deed of settlement, kubaliyat or rent receipt and could not show the basis of SA khatian in any manner, but the courts below on an speculation observed that somehow Azahar Ali Mridha obtained the property by way of pattan, consequently, SA khatian recorded in his name which has no basis at all. 

 11. He further argued that both the courts below put stress on the proceeding under Rules 30 and 31 of the SAT Rules initiated. by Azahar Ali Mridha in the year 1980, but in our jurisdiction it has been decided that unless the title of the plaintiff is invaded no cause Of action for filing suit arises. In the instant case after publication of RS khatian finally, the plaintiff came to know about wrong record and by such wrong record title of the plaintiffs have become clouded then they filed the present suit. 

 13. Finally, he argued that by any record-of-right in particular recording of name of a person in SA and RS khatian having no basis at all, the defendants acquired no title in the suit property. In support of his such submission he has referred to a catena of cases Syed Abdul Hague and another vs Surendra Nath Majumder and others reported in IV ADC, 43, Lal Meah vs Haji Md. Ibrahim Meah and others reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61, Narendra Chandra Das and another vs Sree Sree Gopal Bigraha and another, reported in 3 XP (AD) 201, Government of Bangladesh vs Abdul Malek reported in 61 DLR 635, Sajeda Khatun and others vs Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 34 BLD (AD) 227, Abdul Aziz and others vs Hindu Deivy Luxmi Gobinda Jew and others reported in BCR 2006 (AD), 214 and Md. Motiruddin Mondal @ Matiar Rahman Mondal and others vs Full Mohammed Mollah and others reported in III ADC, 108. 

 14. It is also argued that as decided by this Court SA khatian has no presumptive value and on the basis of SA Khatian nobody acquires title in the property, but both the courts below in one hand failed to appreciate the provisions of law, misread and misconstrued the evidences on record, as such, committed illegality and error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 16. He submits that SA khatian correctly recorded in the name of Azahar Ali Mridha as agricultural tenant under Rezia Khatun as appearing from SA khatian itself. It is argued that since 1957 the predecessor of defendants have been paying rents to the government continuously as tenant under the government, no objection whatever from plaintiffs or their predecessor Rezia Khatun ever raised till 1980. 

 17. He submits that cause of action for filing of the suit lastly arises in the year 1980 when Azahar Ali Mridha filed objection case before the Settlement Officer in respect of wrong recording of name of Rezia Khatun at the backside of khatian which was sustained and accordingly, draft RS khatian was corrected, then Rezia Khatun filed appeal under Rule 31 of the SAT Rules which was rejected. The petitioners or their predecessor Rezia Khatun ought to have agitated the matter before the civil court within six years from rejection of the appeal on 15-5-1980, but after her death and after long time the plaintiffs filed this suit for simple declaration, as such, both the courts below rightly found that the suit is hopelessly time barred. 

 21. He submits that a portion of the property has been acquired by the government for construction of highway, acquisition notice was issued in the name of predecessor of the defendants and compensation award made in the name of Azahar Ali Mridha. Had the plaintiffs owned the property by inheritance from Rezia Khatun or Rezia Khatun had title in the property SA Khatian RS Khatian, and the notice for compensation would have been prepared and issued in the name of plaintiffs or their predecessor. Both the courts below considered series of exhibits filed by the defendants and finally found that the defendants are in possession and there was reasonable cause for preparing SA khatian and RS khatian in the name of Azahar Ali Mridha, as such, both the courts below committed no illegality or error of law in the, decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 23. As admitted by both the parties the property in question along with vast property was purchased by predecessor of the plaintiffs Rezia Khatun by sale deeds dated 20-3-1944 and 5-5-1945. The plaintiffs claimed that predecessor of defendants Azahar Ali Mridha since closely related to predecessor of the plaintiffs, Rezia Khatun was entrusted to look after the property owned by Rezia Khatun and to get the record prepared in her name and payment of rents to the government. Taking advantage of having control and management of the property he with ulterior motive got the SA khatian recorded in his name for the suit plots measuring 66 sataks and also claimed that Azahar Ali Mridha was not raiyat under Rezia Khatun and he was not settled with the suit property by any settlement or issuing any rent receipt by Rezia Khatun. 

 24. To appreciate the argument and the statement made by the petitioners. I have gone through the plaint in suit as well as judgment and order passed in Appeal Case No. 7163 of 1980. (Exhibit-Umo-3). From perusal of Exhibit-Umo-3, it appears that Rezia Khatun before the Appeal Officer claimed that predecessor of defendants Azahar Ali Mridha was borgader under her who used to cultivate the land before SA operation and at that time Rezia Khatun was out of that area. He had no adult son, consequently, she entrusted elder brother of her husband named Bilat Ali to look after the property on her behalf and to prepare SA khatian in her name. Bilat Ali informed her that SA khatian correctly recorded in her name, but she could not take any information about truthness of the fact as said by Bilat Ali and she came to know from objection case filed by Azahar Ali Mridha against draft khatian, which contradicts the statement made in the plaint by the plaintiffs and made before the Appeal Officer by the predecessor of the plaintiffs. 

 26. From the aforesaid observations made by the Appeal Officer, it is found that Azahar Ali Mridha produced cheque dakhila before the Settlement Officer and Appeal Officer showing payment of rents to Rezia Khatun. Modified SA Khatian No. 1364/1 (Exhibit-Ka) supports the observations made by the Appeal Officer which was modified under Section 46 of the SAT Act, 1950 recognizing Azahar Ali Mridha as direct tenant under the government showing Rezia Khatun owner of the property as landlord under her Azahar Ali Mridha was agricultural tenant. Therefore, contention of the petitioners that the SA khatian has no basis at all has no substance and fact of acquiring title as agricultural tenant under Rezia Khatun was established in objection case and appeal case and it was also established that Azahar Ali Mridha was in possession. Fact of the cases referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioners regarding basis of SA and RS khatian are totally different from the fact of the present case. Both the courts below concurrently observed and found that recording of SA khatian and RS khatian in the name of Azahar Ali Mridha has basis and the documents like rent receipts showing payment of rents right from 1957 till today (Exhibit-Kha series), judgment and order of the Appeal Officer (Exhibit Umo-3), Advocate Commissioner report (Exhibit-Chha), notice of acquisition of property (Exhibits Umo-1 and 2) and the evidences led by defendants as DWs all corroborate each other supporting title of the defendants in the suit property.
